dialog.body: Public Works, good morning, this is Lorraine.

Yeah, morning. This is Nilson Pina, I'm at 18 Howard Street, Fifth Ward, down by the corner with the, uh, hold on, let me just put this, okay. The drain. The catch basin at the corner. It did it again.
Okay, Mr. Pina. 18 Howard Street. And this is the catch basin at the corner by your house backing up?
Backing up, overflowing, whatever you want to call it. The rain Friday into Saturday, it came right up over the grate, onto the sidewalk, the whole street was a pond. Right up to my top step. Again.
Up to your top step. Okay. Let me pull up the address, I think I've got some history here. [pause] Yes, okay, I see it. I actually spoke with your son back in February, I think. Wilson?
That's him, yeah. That was after the second one. So you know. You know what's been going on.

I've got it in front of me. So I have a call from you on January twelfth, after the storm that weekend, and then the call from Wilson on February twenty-second, and one from your wife the next evening.

Right. Three calls. And now this is four. Hang on, I got, sorry, I'm moving boxes around here, I'm not ignoring you. [pause] Okay. So the January storm, the big coastal one, water in the basement. Then the nor'easter at the end of February, water in the basement again, worse. Two times this winter. I'm not exaggerating. Two times.
I see both of those noted. Two inches the first time, and about five inches the second time, is that right?

Five inches, yeah. And this time, okay, this time it stayed dry. Basement's dry. But I'm telling you, it's not because anything's fixed. It's because I sat up all night watching it. I had the pump down there, hose ready, plugged in, ready to go, and I'm standing at the front window every twenty minutes like a, like I don't know what. All night Friday.
So you were up all night with a pump ready to go, and the water came up on the sidewalk, but none got into the basement this time.
None got in. Thank God. But it was close. It was right there.
Okay. And can you tell me what the basin itself looked like? Was the grate covered?

Covered? It was buried. Leaves. Packed in leaves, wet leaves, like a mat on top of it. The water had nowhere to go. It just sat there and spread. Saturday morning I went out with a rake and pulled a pile off it myself, like a, hold on. [pause] Sorry. Like a garbage bag full. Off one grate.
Buried in leaves, water had nowhere to go, and you raked it off Saturday morning. I'm putting all of that in.

See, that's the thing. In January the crew comes, they clean off the top, they shovel a little around it, done. Then in February they come back, they do the, the jet thing, under the corner, and the guy tells my son it was partly blocked. Partly blocked. Okay. So now it's cleared, great, and then two weeks later it's full of leaves again? Nobody's coming by to keep it clean? It's March. Where are all these leaves even coming from?
I understand. I do see the crew visit on January thirteenth where they cleared the grate, and then February twenty-fourth when they jetted the line and found it partly blocked.

And then the supervisor calls my son, calls my wife, same day, says they're looking at a bigger fix. Looking at it. No date, nothing. So I'm asking you, what's the date? When does anybody actually do something so I can sleep when it rains?

I hear you. I don't have a date on the bigger fix in here. What I can do is add this weekend's backup to the repeat file for your corner, with the leaves and the water up to your step, and I'll send it straight to the supervisor today so it's in front of them, not just sitting in the system.

The repeat file. Okay. [pause] Can I ask you something? Is it just me? Like, does the city have any record of anybody else on Howard calling about this? Because I can't be the only house. My neighbor across, I saw him out there too with a broom Saturday.

Let me look. Give me one second. [pause] Okay, I'm searching the street. I'm seeing your household's calls come up most. I don't see a separate report from another number on Howard for this weekend, at least not one that's been entered yet. Things from the weekend are still getting put in this morning, so that could change.

So it's just us calling. Great. Everybody else just sweeps and goes inside. You know what, I'll tell him to call. Tell him to call you. Because if it's only one house it looks like one guy complaining, right?
It does help when more people on the street report it, yes. If your neighbor wants to call, he can give his own address and say it's the same corner basin. That'll tie it together.

Okay. Okay. Oh, and another thing, while I got you. Saturday morning I get a text on my phone. Some alert or something. Not in English. I don't know what language, I couldn't read a word of it. Was that you guys? Was that the city telling me something about the storm?
Hmm. Did it come from a short number, like five or six digits, or a regular phone number?
I don't know, I deleted it, I thought it was junk. Now I'm thinking, what if that was the warning? What if they're warning everybody and I'm getting it in some language I don't even speak?

I can't tell you for sure what that was. I'm going to note it, and I'll ask our office that handles the alert sign-ups whether anything went out Saturday and whether your number's set to the wrong language. If it is, that's something they can fix. If it wasn't us, it was probably junk.

Okay. Yeah. Please. Because that's one more thing, you know? I'm up all night, I'm raking leaves, I'm getting texts I can't read. [pause] Sorry, I'm not yelling at you. You've been good. I'm just tired of this. Thirty-eight years in this house, and this winter it's like every rain I gotta stand guard.

No, I understand. Let me read back what I've got so it's right. 18 Howard Street. Rain Friday into Saturday, the corner catch basin overflowed onto the sidewalk and the street ponded to your top step. The basin was buried in leaves. You watched it overnight with a pump ready and the basement stayed dry this time. Basement flooded twice already this winter, January and late February. You'd like a date on the larger fix, and the question about the text in another language. Is that everything?
That's everything. And put down that somebody needs to come clean the leaves off it before the next one. Not after. Before.
I'll put that in: request to clear the basin before the next rain. I can't book a crew date myself on this, but it goes to the supervisor with the rest of it today.
Okay. Do they have my number? Same one as before?
I have the number ending in oh-one-three-one on the file. Is that still good?
That's me, yeah. That's the one.
Good. Then that's where they'll reach you.
Alright. I'll be waiting. Again. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Mr. Pina. Try to get some sleep.
